title: Collection of ultrasound cross sectional images from healthy volunteers for machine learning to develop real time segmentation and classification of organs
summary:
This project collects a new set of high quality ultrasound pictures from healthy volunteers. The goal is to help computer programs learn to recognize and outline organs quickly, so that future ultrasound exams can be easier to perform and easier to learn.

At the moment, many existing ultrasound image collections are limited. They may be too small, of mixed quality, wrongly labeled, or focused only on people who are already ill. Images from healthy people are important as a normal reference, and these are often missing.

About 50 healthy adults aged 18 or older will take part. Participation involves one ultrasound appointment that lasts about 20 to 25 minutes. Before the scan, a few basic details are recorded, such as age, height, weight, sex, and relevant health history. During the scan, the study team takes ultrasound pictures of several organs in the belly area. Participants can also choose to have extra pictures taken of the thyroid gland.

The scan uses sound waves, not radiation, and it does not break the skin, nor causes any harm. The collected images and basic information are stored with a study code on a secure server, so they cannot be directly linked to a person. The data will be used to develop and test computer programs for organ recognition, organ measurements, report generation, and to support scientific research and publications.

The ultrasound exam will be performed by experienced medical staff (DEGUM Stufe 3).

There is no direct medical benefit for participants, but the work may benefit future patients and medical staff by improving ultrasound tools and training.
conditions: Healthy volunteers for the collection of baseline ultrasound data and the establishment of valid reference and baseline values for the development of real time segmentation algorithms and automated report generation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy volunteers aged 18 years or older who are able to provide informed consent. Women of childbearing potential are eligible regardless of contraception use, as diagnostic ultrasound is non invasive and involves no radiation exposure or additional risk related to pregnancy status.
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years or inability to provide informed consent. Participants with conditions or organ related abnormalities that would prevent standardized ultrasound acquisition of the target organs are excluded, as are patients.
